# TableSeed

A hash seed, drawn once and shared by every table that wants one.

```rux
pub struct TableSeed {
    // private fields
}
```

Two words, which is what `SipHash` takes as a key. Drawing one per table costs a system call each; a program
making many should draw one and hand it to all of them, which is what this being a value rather than a hidden
global is for.

## Associated functions

<h3 id="random"><code>Random</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Random() -> TableSeed
```

A seed drawn from the operating system.
Takes nothing. Falls back to a fixed pair of words when the system has no entropy to give, which keeps a
table working on a system without a generator at the cost of the protection the seed exists for — a table
keyed on adversarial input on such a system is as attackable as an unseeded one.
Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

**Returns**: a seed drawn from the system, so two tables in one process iterate differently

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Collections/Src/Table.rux#L62)

<h3 id="of"><code>Of</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Of(low: uint64, high: uint64) -> TableSeed
```

A seed with the words a caller chose.
`low` and `high` are read by value. For a test that needs the same table twice, or a caller drawing one seed
for many tables.

| Name   | Type     | Description         |
| ------ | -------- | ------------------- |
| `low`  | `uint64` | the first seed word |
| `high` | `uint64` | the second          |

**Returns**: a seed made of those two words, which makes the iteration order reproducible

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Collections/Src/Table.rux#L75)
